issues.text: Submitting the Cloud waitlist form with visitor@example.com shows the visible error “Could not join waitlist.” The submission request POST /api/waitlist returned HTTP 501.

Submitting the Cloud waitlist form with a valid email provides a visitor-facing submission result. — The email field was filled with “visitor@example.com” (steps 4–5) and Join waitlist was clicked (step 5), but no confirmation, error, navigation, or other submission outcome was observed; the final observation explicitly records a “waitlist submission failure” (step 24).

Clicking the “What can I do with MCP?” FAQ item expands it and reveals its answer. — The MCP item was clicked repeatedly (steps 21–23), each attempt recorded domChanged=NO; the preceding observation still showed the CI FAQ answer rather than an MCP answer (step 21), and the final page showed the MCP item collapsed with a plus icon (step 24).
Cloud waitlist signup cannot be completed: submitting a populated valid email address displays “Could not join waitlist.” and the POST /api/waitlist request returns HTTP 501.

Submitting a valid email address through the Cloud waitlist form successfully joins the waitlist. — After entering visitor@example.com and clicking Join waitlist (steps 4-5), the next observation records that a waitlist failure remained displayed beneath the populated field (step 6).

Each visible FAQ accordion, including “What can I do with MCP?”, expands to reveal its answer when clicked. — Several FAQ items expanded and displayed answers (steps 15-22), but repeated clicks on the visible MCP row left its plus icon and no answer visible even after scrolling it fully into view (steps 24-27).

The Cloud waitlist form rejects a syntactically valid email address (visitor@example.com) with the visible message “Could not join waitlist.” The submission request to /api/waitlist returned HTTP 501.
Blog navigation active styling is missing on the initial /blog/ visit but appears after returning to the same page.

Clicking the visible “August 5, 2026 Evidence-First CI: Proving Every Pull Request” article card opens the article page. — Step 2 directly clicked the article link but recorded domChanged=NO and no destination page or article content was observed afterward.
